business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Vertical integration is the stated core of the model: the management team and the assets are housed under a single corporate structure rather than the traditional fragmented development-manager/operating model, which the RHP states removes management-fee leakage and manager-owner conflict and speeds decision-making. It describes itself as the only scaled pure-play industrial and logistics platform combining real estate, infrastructure and operational services under one roof (Source: JLL Report). Downstream of the shell, the Company bundles an ecosystem into the same customer relationship: turnkey development with capital-expenditure and fit-out solutions for select customers with demonstrated credit quality and long-term commitments (stated to enhance overall realization), rooftop solar energy solutions monetizing its own roof footprint (21.31 MW operational, 17.20 MW being installed), on-site staff accommodation and CII-partnered skill development centers, cold storage developed with in-house execution expertise, racking and material handling equipment, and an under-development hospitality offering. In-house engineering and technical capability supports execution of complex industrial projects to Grade A+ specifications with cost discipline. Upstream, the network was assembled through acquisitions (32 of 45 assets, 62.00% of Total Network, from Promoters and their related entities), greenfield development and strategic redevelopment, alongside joint ventures and government partnerships. The RHP states this compresses customer time-to-market to approximately six to nine months versus the typical 24 to 30 months when a customer manages all aspects independently (Source: JLL Report).

opportunities: Embedded organic pipeline: approximately 30.03 msf of developable potential (Near Term Deliveries and Planned Projects) on existing, fully paid land bank, to be built out over the next four to five years.

In-city expansion runway: continued expansion through the Central Warehousing Corporation relationship and other governmental authorities across Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bangalore, Pune, Nagpur and Goa; three urban distribution centres under development in the NCR Delhi region with 1.3 msf combined potential.
Mark-to-market on lease expiry: re-pricing opportunity on renewal, evidenced by the 11.71% spread achieved on 4.78 msf re-leased or renewed since Fiscal 2024 (proforma).
Sector under-penetration: India's Grade A and Grade B warehousing and industrial stock stood at 548.9 msf as of March 2026, less than half of Chicago's 1.3 billion sq ft (JLL Report).

Sector growth: combined Grade A and B stock reached 531.6 msf as of CY2025, having expanded at a 15.6% CAGR between CY2020 and CY2025, with Grade A occupancy expected to expand a further 440 bps to 96.8% (JLL Report).

Manufacturing, consumption and e-commerce tailwinds; plug-and-play leasing economics cited to cut occupier capital expenditure by up to 42% and operating expenditure by up to 20%; record institutional investment into Indian real estate.

Strategic expansion into new segments for deeper value-chain integration, plus continued land and asset acquisition (large contiguous parcels typically of 50-100 acres, and brownfield turnaround acquisitions).
Institutional-backed Grade A development pipeline of 250.1 msf of potential leasable area nationally, indicating a formalising and institutionalising market (JLL Report).
strengths: Largest player by scale: Total Network of 58.58 msf across 45 assets in 10 cities as of the date of the RHP; India's largest industrial and logistics infrastructure developer, owner and operator by Total Network as of May 2026 (JLL Report).

Only scaled pure-play industrial and logistics platform combining real estate, infrastructure and operational services under one roof (JLL Report); no listed comparable exists in India or the seven named economies.

Premium Grade A+ specification network: 12-metre clear heights, 12-metre-wide roads and 16-metre-wide aprons for 40-foot trailers, K160/K115 sprinkler fire protection, skylights, ridge monitors, louvers and insulation.

Unrivalled in-city portfolio: 17 in-city centers with 6.91 msf potential, the largest among peers (JLL Report), reaching over 20 million end-consumers within a 10-30 minute drive; 13 sites secured from Central Warehousing Corporation on 45-year concessions, against high barriers to entry for others.

Geographic diversification across India's top 10 markets (Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai, Pune, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Nagpur, Nashik, Goa), which represent approximately 9% of India's population, contribute approximately 21% of GDP and have approximately 3x the national average per-capita income as of March 2026 (JLL Report).

Customer quality and diversification: 118 customers as of May 31, 2026 across consumption (e-commerce, q-commerce, 3PL, FMCG, retail) and manufacturing segments; 54.05% of committed Operational Network contracted to Fortune 500 companies.

Demonstrated pricing power and asset management: 7.69% CAGR in gross rental per sq ft per month from April 1, 2023 to May 31, 2026; 4.78 msf re-leased or renewed between Fiscal 2024 and May 31, 2026 at an 11.71% spread over the prior contracts (proforma); contractual escalations of 4.5%-5.0% per annum or 15% every three years.
Committed Occupancy maintained above 89% since FY21; national Grade A occupancy 92.4% in CY2025 (JLL Report).

Execution and development capability: 11.93 msf of new facilities delivered across 19 assets between Fiscal 2024 and May 31, 2026 (proforma); in-house development team of 120 personnel as of May 31, 2026.
Sustainability standing: 5-Star GRESB rating with a participation score above 90 in its inaugural assessment; 91.85% of Operational Network IGBC Platinum certified as of May 31, 2026.

Promoter backing: Promoters are part of the Blackstone Group, with more than 1.2 billion sq ft of logistics holdings globally as of September 30, 2025 and more than 20 years of operating experience in India.
threats: Competition may increase if competitors open new facilities or expand offerings, including customers or potential customers choosing to use their own facilities (Risk Factor 35); competes with international and domestic institutional developers and large regional developers.

Competition from the Promoters' own affiliates: affiliates of the Promoters have entered into and may in future enter into arrangements to invest in other Indian logistics and warehousing companies with similar investment strategies, resulting in direct competition and potential conflict of interest, with no exclusivity arrangement in place (Risk Factors 14 and 22).

Land scarcity and increasing competition for land in Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Chennai, Bangalore and Pune; much of the available land is classified as agricultural and requires land-use conversion involving regulatory hurdles, time and cost (Risk Factor 9).
Supply-demand imbalance: over-supply in specific sub-markets can raise vacancy rates and stabilise rents (JLL 'Potential Threats and Challenges').
Inflation in land, construction material, labour and utility costs affecting new project feasibility and existing asset profitability (JLL).

Trade policy and tariff risk: trade disputes, new tariffs or global supply-chain changes can alter export-import volumes and distribution patterns and cause customers to defer or recalibrate expansion plans (JLL; Risk Factors).

Regulatory and policy change: the Delhi Draft Logistics and Warehousing Policy 2025 proposes relocating warehouses from congested city areas to the periphery, which could require relocation, retrofitting or operational modification, and similar policies may follow in other states (JLL) - a direct threat to the in-city strategy.
Restrictive zoning and approval delays extending development timelines and increasing financing costs (JLL).

Occupancy dependence: financial performance depends on maintaining high Committed Occupancy, with the competitiveness of rental rates relative to other Grade A properties in the same micro-markets a named determinant (Risk Factor 36).
Land may be subject to acquisition or eminent domain by governments and regulatory authorities, with potentially inadequate compensation (Risk Factor 20).
A credit rating downgrade could restrict access to capital and raise borrowing costs (Risk Factor 28).

Real estate illiquidity: limited ability to vary or liquidate assets in response to changing economic or property market conditions, dependent on competition from other sellers and buyer financing availability.
Reputational contagion from the Blackstone-affiliated Promoters' diverse global interests (Risk Factor 22).
Reliance on the JLL Report, which the Company exclusively commissioned and paid for and which neither the Company nor the BRLMs nor any other person connected with the Issue has verified.
weaknesses: Loss-making: restated consolidated losses of Rs. 2,036.49 million (FY2026), Rs. 1,787.81 million (FY2025) and Rs. 1,622.10 million (FY2024); proforma losses of Rs. 1,908.20 million, Rs. 2,394.27 million and Rs. 2,750.70 million for the same fiscals (Risk Factor 2).

Negative Return on Net Worth throughout: restated (4.23%) FY2026, (136.35%) FY2025, (59.46%) FY2024; proforma (4.09%), (19.30%), (23.93%).

No listed-peer benchmark for pricing: the RHP itself warns that the absence of directly comparable publicly available information 'may affect investors' ability to assess our relative performance and industry position', and that the valuation would not be benchmarked against industry peers.

Substantial indebtedness requiring significant cash flows to service and limiting operating freedom (Risk Factor 12); Rs. 22,500.00 million of Net Proceeds earmarked for repayment or prepayment of borrowings.
Customer concentration: the top 10 customers accounted for 42.60%, 43.12% and 54.04% of proforma revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
Geographic concentration: Delhi-NCR, Chennai, Bangalore and Pune together contributed 79.00%, 79.79% and 87.67% of proforma revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.

Execution-heavy asset base: the Development Network of 30.03 msf is 51.26% of Total Network as of May 31, 2026 (7.22 msf Near Term Deliveries, 22.81 msf Planned Projects), subject to construction delay and cost risk; the Operational Network is only 28.55 msf (48.74%).
A significant portion of the network was acquired from the Promoters and other sellers recently, in Fiscals 2025 and 2026 (Risk Factor 1).
Some Subsidiaries, including Material Subsidiary Volumnus Developers Private Limited, have had negative net worth and may continue to (Risk Factor 27).

Audit reports on the Restated Consolidated Financial Information and the assurance report on the Proforma Financial Information carry emphasis-of-matter paragraphs and CARO 2020 observations (Risk Factor 18).

Title and development rights over the land on which assets are located may be subject to legal uncertainties and defects (Risk Factor 8); certain assets and the Registered and Corporate Office are leased (Risk Factor 15).
Reliance on independent contractors for the construction of assets (Risk Factor 10).

overview.business_model: The Company develops, acquires, owns and operates Grade A fulfillment centers (warehouses), industrial facilities and in-city centers for corporate customers across India's major industrial and consumption hubs, offering built-to-suit facilities, fully fitted plug-and-play facilities, cold storage, energy solutions, on-site staff accommodation and racking and material handling equipment. Its main objects permit it to build, own, operate, sell or lease industrial and business parks and warehouses and to provide logistics and facility-management services. As of May 31, 2026 the Operational Network was 28.55 msf (fulfillment centers 16.34 msf, industrial facilities 11.42 msf, in-city centers 0.79 msf) at Committed Occupancy of 93.56% (91.58% / 95.94% / 100.00% respectively), which indicates a leasing/occupancy-driven model. The network was assembled through acquisitions (32 of the 45 assets, 36.32 msf or 62.00% of Total Network, from the Promoters and their related entities), greenfield development and targeted redevelopment. strategy_growth.detail: RF9. Supply of land in Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Chennai, Bangalore and Pune is limited and contested (JLL Report), and available land is often agricultural, requiring land use conversion with regulatory hurdles, time and cost. New in-city centers face high barriers to entry from competing land use and elevated real estate costs, with freehold land in city limits typically better suited to residential or commercial offices given better floor space index utilisation, so in-city logistics stock is limited. Due diligence and acquisition costs may be incurred even where an acquisition does not proceed, and land allotment approval from government authorities does not guarantee immediate possession.

concerns_observed: Loss-making in each of the three years presented, on both bases: restated loss for the year Rs (2,036.49) mn (FY26), Rs (1,787.81) mn (FY25), Rs (1,622.10) mn (FY24); proforma loss Rs (1,908.20) / (2,394.27) / (2,750.70) mn. Restated RoNW was negative throughout at (4.23%) / (136.35%) / (59.46%), weighted average (57.47%); proforma RoNW (4.09%) / (19.30%) / (23.93%), weighted average (12.46%). No dividend was paid in Fiscals 2026, 2025 or 2024 or up to the RHP date.

Finance cost consumes most of the revenue line: restated finance costs Rs 5,389.92 / 3,528.94 / 2,108.31 mn were 77.96% / 90.42% / 92.12% of revenue from operations in FY26 / FY25 / FY24, and depreciation and amortisation a further 38.49% / 36.71% / 42.89%. On the proforma basis finance costs were 68.88% / 75.03% / 83.60% of proforma total income. Debt service coverage is 1.16 times restated (1.15 times proforma) and interest service 1.36 times (1.35 times).

62.00% of the network came from the Promoters themselves, almost all of it in the last two years: 32 of the 45 assets, 36.32 msf, were acquired from the Promoters and their related entities, of which 25 assets / 19.41 msf in Fiscal 2025 and 6 assets / 14.35 msf in Fiscal 2026, against just 1 asset / 2.56 msf before Fiscal 2025. The RHP states there can be no assurance those transactions could not have been done on different terms had they not been with related parties.

Three quarters of the growth pipeline has barely broken ground: of the 30.03 msf Development Network (51.26% of Total Network as of May 31, 2026), 22.81 msf are Planned Projects on which less than 1.00% of construction has been completed, with delivery expected over four to five years. Even within the 7.22 msf of Near Term Deliveries, completion as of May 31, 2026 runs as low as 5.00% at Koka (0.18 msf), Bhiwandi (0.77 msf) and Sahibabad I (0.25 msf).

The Company does not meet the ordinary IPO eligibility test: monetary assets were 57.39% of net tangible assets as at March 31, 2025 against the 50% limit in Regulation 6(1)(a) of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, and neither the Company nor its Subsidiaries utilised or made firm commitments to utilise the excess, which stood at 45.22% as at March 31, 2026. The Issue therefore proceeds under Regulation 6(2), with not less than 75% of the Net Issue allotted to QIBs and the QIB Portion not underwritten.

Revenue is concentrated on a handful of customers and four cities: top 10 customers were 42.60% of proforma revenue from operations in FY26 (Rs 2,945.06 mn), 43.12% in FY25 and 54.04% in FY24, with Instakart Services Private Limited alone at Rs 768.51 mn or 11.12% in FY26 (12.01% FY25, 15.93% FY24); Delhi-NCR, Chennai, Bangalore and Pune produced Rs 5,461.85 mn or 79.00% of proforma revenue in FY26 (79.79% FY25, 87.67% FY24), Delhi-NCR alone 33.58%. Three of the top ten customers are unnamed because consent to disclose was not given.

The two bases the RHP runs in parallel diverge sharply in the earlier years and the issuer itself limits reliance on the proforma one: proforma revenue from operations was Rs 6,094.23 mn (FY25) and Rs 4,528.51 mn (FY24) against restated Rs 3,902.86 mn and Rs 2,288.61 mn, and proforma revenue growth reads 13.45% / 34.57% against restated 77.15% / 70.53%. The Proforma Financial Information assumes the Acquisition Transactions took effect from April 1, 2023 or the date of incorporation if later, and the RHP states it addresses a hypothetical situation and that 'the degree of reliance placed by investors on our Proforma Financial Information should be limited'.

Committed Occupancy fell before it recovered, and the fall coincided with the largest intake of assets: proforma Committed Occupancy dropped to 89.88% at March 31, 2026 from 93.94% at March 31, 2025 while the Operational Network grew from 23.31 msf to 28.42 msf, recovering to 93.56% by May 31, 2026. On the restated basis the same metric reads 91.76% (FY24), 92.58% (FY25), 89.88% (FY26).

Audit-trail and books-of-account exceptions run across the holding company and dozens of subsidiaries in both audited years. For the year ended March 31, 2026 the auditors state they are unable to comment on the audit trail at database level for the Holding Company and 35 subsidiaries for want of SOC reports, and that the database-level audit trail to log direct data changes was not enabled throughout the year for 12 subsidiaries. For the year ended March 31, 2025 the back-up of electronic books of account was not kept daily on servers physically located in India for the Holding Company and 31 subsidiaries, and the prior-year audit trail was not preserved for 4 subsidiaries and 14 newly incorporated subsidiaries.

Litigation sits mostly one level down, and nothing is provided for: against the Subsidiaries there are 27 material civil litigations, 17 tax proceedings and 4 statutory or regulatory actions aggregating Rs 932.11 million; against the Company 2 tax and 2 material civil matters aggregating Rs 46.36 million; by the Subsidiaries 1 criminal and 4 material civil matters aggregating Rs 501.41 million. The Company states no provisions have been made for these outstanding matters. The Materiality Threshold adopted is Rs 90.77 million, being 5% of average absolute PAT of the preceding three years, the lowest of the three tests (2% of turnover Rs 138.28 million; 2% of net worth Rs 935.23 million).

Land title is the structural weakness of the asset base: for certain parcels the Company states it is 'unable to trace the title devolution for periods up to 30 years prior to the acquisition of such land parcels by us', relying instead on revenue records (patta, 7/12 extract, property cards, jamabandis) which the RHP itself says may not be reliable. Named defects include 8.71 of the 14.77 acres at Horizon Industrial Park MWC categorised as 'Anadheenam' with restrictions on conveyance, transfer and mortgage, and 41.51 acres at Horizon Industrial Park Chakan V categorised as forest land pending re-categorisation by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

The CWC concession block, which underpins the in-city strategy, is under challenge: C.W.P. No. 16416 of 2025, filed September 24, 2025 by the Federation of Central Warehousing Corporation Employees Unions before the High Court of Delhi, contests the asset monetisation of CWC warehouses allotted to BRE Asia III India Holdings Ltd (since amalgamated into the Company) and names three Alotrion/Alotronix subsidiaries; the RHP quantifies no amount. Separately, the appointed date under the CWC concessions for four of the 13 assets, measuring 1.24 msf of Total Network, is still contingent on CWC completing conditions precedent.

Statutory dues were paid late repeatedly, at scale in Fiscal 2025: TDS delays of Rs 96.36 million across 48 instances with an average delay of 112 days in FY25, Rs 8.46 million across 37 instances averaging 58 days in FY26 and Rs 6.79 million across 13 instances averaging 115 days in FY24; GST Rs 37.64 million across 53 instances (FY25) and Rs 41.40 million across 11 instances (FY24); professional tax of Rs 0.01 million in a single FY25 instance delayed 467 days; EPF Rs 0.33 million across 5 FY26 instances averaging 50 days. Unpaid dues are stated as Nil in every printed cell.

FEMA form-filing non-compliance is partly unremedied at the RHP date: late submission fees of Rs 0.13 million were paid for delayed RBI filings on allotments of Equity Shares across Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, and Rs 1.89 million for delayed Form FCTRS (four Subsidiaries) and Form DI (35 Subsidiaries) filings pursuant to the Merger Transactions. For two Subsidiaries acquired through the Merger Transactions, filings required from their erstwhile shareholders remain pending with the RBI, and the Company states its own filings for those entities can be completed only once those prior delays are resolved.

Negative net worth is widespread across the operating subsidiaries even after the restructuring: as of March 31, 2026 net assets were negative at LI Industrial Parks Rs (1,605.03) mn, Embassy Industrial Park Hosur Rs (1,416.85) mn, Panvel Logistics and Warehousing Solutions Rs (690.47) mn, Panvel Warehousing Rs (575.93) mn, Malur Logistics Rs (503.83) mn, Kalina Warehousing Rs (298.03) mn and others; Material Subsidiary Volumnus Developers was negative in FY25 and FY24 before turning positive at Rs 454.84 mn in FY26.

Capital commitments dwarf the contingent liabilities and keep rising: estimated contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for, net of advances, were Rs 12,640.49 million (FY26) against Rs 9,806.36 million (FY25) and Rs 5,622.22 million (FY24), alongside contingent liabilities of Rs 503.80 million at March 31, 2026 (GST matters Rs 502.22 million, income tax Rs 1.58 million) versus Rs 688.87 million at March 31, 2025 and Nil at March 31, 2024.

The pool identified for repayment is roughly twice the amount that will be applied, and the RHP does not allocate it: the identified borrowings of the Company and the 16 Identified Subsidiaries stood at Rs 58,884.50 million sanctioned and Rs 46,821.13 million outstanding as of March 31, 2026, against Rs 22,500.00 million of Net Proceeds earmarked; the RHP expressly reserves the right to avail additional facilities, repay instalments or refinance any listed loan after filing, so which loans are actually repaid is at management's discretion.

The debt that remains is floating and repo/MCLR-linked while lease rentals escalate on fixed contractual formulas: variable-rate borrowings were Rs 67,661.40 million at March 31, 2026 under the Ind AS 107 market-risk note, with rates of 8.30% to 9.10% p.a. on the Company's borrowings and 7.39% to 9.85% on the Subsidiaries', 'primarily linked and subject to changes in the various interest rate benchmarks such as the repo rate prescribed by the RBI, treasury bill rate and MCLR of the specific lender plus a spread', against contractual rent escalations of 4.5%-5.0% per annum or 15% every three years.

The bulk of the proceeds benefits the subsidiaries rather than the issuer, as the RHP concedes: because the primary beneficiaries of the repayment object are the Identified Subsidiaries, the RHP states there can be no assurance of any significant improvement in the Company's standalone profitability or cash flows. The Objects have not been appraised by any bank, financial institution or any other independent agency, and the general corporate purposes amount is [bullet], capped at 25% of Gross Proceeds.

Part of the repayment flows to associates of two of the five BRLMs: facilities of seven Subsidiaries owed to State Bank of India and Axis Bank Limited, associates of SBI Capital Markets Limited and Axis Capital Limited respectively, sit in the repayment pool — Farukhnagar Logistics Parks LLP Rs 5,189.24 mn and Embassy Industrial Park Hosur Rs 2,949.98 mn and Malur Logistics Rs 2,929.62 mn and Patancheru Industrial Park Rs 743.23 mn to SBI; FRK II Industrial Park Rs 4,072.50 mn, Goodluck Buildtech Rs 1,547.89 mn and Rs 130.23 mn, and Jindpur Industrial Park Rs 904.16 mn to Axis Bank (outstanding as of March 31, 2026). The RHP states these are not associates of the Company under the SEBI Merchant Bankers Regulations but concedes the repayment may be perceived as a conflict of interest.

Compulsory acquisition has already been finalised over part of the land bank: by notification dated March 18, 2026 under Section 28(4) of the KIAD Act, the Government of Karnataka finalised 31.625 acres held by Banamakanahalli Industrial and Logistics Private Limited at Hoskote for acquisition; no Section 28(6) notice to hand over possession has been received and the Subsidiary is evaluating remedies. A further 9.656 acres (Volumnus Developers) and 1.85 acres (Vadakkupattu Industrial Parks) at Oragadam are also sought.

Three material approvals have been applied for and not received as of the RHP date — environmental clearance for the expansion of the under-construction portion of Horizon Industrial Park Bilaspur, the occupancy certificate for block C phase II of Horizon Industrial Parks Chakan II, and consent to operate for Greenbase Horizon Industrial Park Oragadam I — and pollution-board notices to Subsidiaries LI Industrial Parks, FRK II Industrial Park and Goodluck Buildtech await final closure letters. The consequence is not hypothetical: in the quarter ended June 30, 2026 a customer served Goodluck Buildtech with a lease termination notice citing delay in handover for want of an occupation certificate, seeking indemnification and refund of security deposit, stamp duty and registration charges.

The statutory auditor changed mid-stream for a stated independence reason: Walker Chandiok & Co LLP resigned on March 5, 2025 because the Company proposed to avail non-audit services that could impair independence; M S K C & Associates LLP was appointed on April 25, 2025 to fill the casual vacancy (re-appointed September 30, 2025) and S G C O & Co. LLP was appointed joint auditor on November 13, 2025. The examination report on the Restated Consolidated Financial Information and the assurance report on the Proforma Financial Information both carry emphasis of matter paragraphs, and Rule 11(g) matters for FY2025 cover audit trail enablement, daily backup, title deeds, disputed statutory dues, short-term funds used for long-term purpose and cash losses of certain Subsidiaries.

The uninsured tail on the one large loss that did occur has not resolved: a flood loss of approximately Rs 394.23 million at Greenbase Horizon Industrial Park Talegaon was recognised under exceptional items in Fiscal 2025, the insurer appointed an independent third-party surveyor, and as of the RHP date no insurance claim receivable has been recognised as an asset.

Governance concentration inside the committees: the Board is six directors with three independent, and the three-member Audit Committee includes the Whole Time Director and Chief Executive Officer whose financial reporting it oversees; the same officer sits on five of the seven committees (Audit, Risk Management, CSR and Sustainability, IPO and Investment), and the Risk Management Committee is chaired by a Non-Executive Director who is not independent. The Promoters hold 2,173,652,861 Equity Shares, 88.74% of pre-Issue paid-up capital, and will retain control after the Issue.

The senior team is thin for a 45-asset, 10-city, 30.03 msf development platform: 3 Key Managerial Personnel and 9 Senior Management Personnel as of May 31, 2026 and March 31, 2026, against 268 total permanent employees at May 31, 2026 (259 in FY26 at 8.11% attrition, 191 in FY25 at 9.95%, 158 in FY24 at 14.56%). The Chief Financial Officer position was filled on October 28, 2025 and the RHP prints no reason for the appointment and discloses no exit of a predecessor.

Construction rests on outside parties: over 40 independent contractors as of May 31, 2026, with the top 10 holding 28.02% of proforma work orders in FY26 (Rs 4,213.03 mn) against 18.97% in FY25 and 21.96% in FY24; contractors hire sub-contractors and on-site contract labour, and the Company may be liable for wage payments or workplace injury compensation on contractor default.

Everything the market is told about the industry and the 'largest' claim comes from a report the Company paid for: the JLL 'Industry Report on India's Industrial & Logistics Sector' dated July 23, 2026 was commissioned and paid for by the Company exclusively for the Issue under an engagement letter of the same date, uses subjective market-sizing and forecasting methodologies, and the RHP states investors may not be able to seek legal recourse for losses resulting from reliance on it.

The Promoters compete with the Company by their own disclosure and there is no restraint: affiliates of the Promoters managed 1.2 billion square feet of logistics assets globally as of September 30, 2025, have entered into and may enter into arrangements to invest in other Indian logistics and warehousing companies, are not prohibited from serving competitors and are under no obligation to direct opportunities to the Company. The RHP states no exclusivity or non-compete arrangements have been entered into with the Promoters.

Recent primary issuance was struck at prices the RHP itself flags as potentially below the Issue Price: a rights issue of 120,200,000 shares at Rs 50 on October 15, 2025; conversion of 299,800,000 OCDs into 50,125,397 shares on December 5, 2025 at a fair value of Rs 59.81; a rights issue of 84,785,153 shares at Rs 59.81 on December 11, 2025; and a preferential allotment of 275,873,599 shares at Rs 59.81 on December 26, 2025 to 25 investors including Radhakishan Damani, SBI Life Insurance, State Bank of India and nine 360 ONE vehicles. Against that, the certified weighted average cost of acquisition for the three Promoters is Rs 29.94, Rs 28.20 and Rs 22.39 per Equity Share.

Policy risk points directly at the in-city portfolio: the Delhi Draft Logistics and Warehousing Policy 2025 proposes relocating warehouses from congested city areas to the periphery, which the RHP states could require relocation, retrofitting or operational modification, with Delhi-NCR carrying fourteen of the 45 assets and 33.58% of FY26 proforma revenue.

Non-GAAP metrics carry a self-declared verification gap: the RHP states EBITDA, EBITDA Margin, Gross External Debt, Net Debt and Total Revenue Growth are not Ind AS, IFRS or US GAAP measures, are not standardised for comparison against other companies, and that operational metrics are prepared with internal systems not independently verified by third parties.

verdict.our_read: Blackstone-promoted industrial and logistics park owner-operator, 58.58 msf across 45 assets and India's largest by Total Network per the commissioned JLL Report, loss-making three years running with FY26 restated finance costs 77.96% of revenue, whose thesis rides on delivering 30.03 msf still undeveloped.

parameter_scores.basis: Restated loss in all three years — Rs (2,036.49) mn FY26, Rs (1,787.81) mn FY25, Rs (1,622.10) mn FY24 — and proforma loss in all three at Rs (1,908.20) / (2,394.27) / (2,750.70) mn. Restated RoNW (4.23%) / (136.35%) / (59.46%), weighted average (57.47%); EPS (1.18) / (3.11) / (2.96) restated and (0.95) / (1.68) / (2.04) proforma. High EBITDA Margin of 79.16% (FY26 restated) is fully absorbed below the line by finance costs of 77.96% of revenue and D&A of 38.49%. No dividend in any of the three years.

Restated total borrowings Rs 68,843.41 mn at March 31, 2026 (proforma Rs 68,867.73 mn) with debt-equity 1.18x restated and 1.22x proforma; consolidated sanctioned Rs 105,843.31 mn against outstanding Rs 68,607.38 mn, net borrowings Rs 42,186.21 mn after Rs 26,421.17 mn of cash, bank balances, liquid investments and DSRA. Variable-rate borrowings Rs 67,661.40 mn are repo/T-bill/MCLR-linked at 8.30%-9.10% (Company) and 7.39%-9.85% (Subsidiaries). Debt service coverage 1.16x, interest service 1.36x. Offsetting: no covenant breach or default notice in FY24-FY26, no rating downgrade, and the Issue is disclosed to take debt-equity to 0.55x.

32 of 45 assets, 36.32 msf or 62.00% of Total Network, were acquired from the Promoters and their related entities — 25 assets / 19.41 msf in Fiscal 2025 and 6 assets / 14.35 msf in Fiscal 2026, against 1 asset / 2.56 msf before Fiscal 2025. The proforma statements that present these as if held from April 1, 2023 are the same statements the RHP says reliance on 'should be limited'. red_flags: The Company does not satisfy Regulation 6(1)(a) of the SEBI ICDR Regulations — monetary assets were 57.39% of net tangible assets as at March 31, 2025 against the 50% ceiling, and neither the Company nor its Subsidiaries utilised or made firm commitments to utilise the excess, which stood at 45.22% as at March 31, 2026 — so the Issue proceeds under Regulation 6(2) with not less than 75% of the Net Issue allotted to QIBs and the QIB Portion not underwritten.

Three consecutive years of losses on both bases, with finance costs at 77.96%, 90.42% and 92.12% of restated revenue from operations in FY26, FY25 and FY24 and negative RoNW throughout — restated (4.23%) / (136.35%) / (59.46%). FY26 EPS is negative on both the restated basis (Rs 1.18) and the proforma basis (Rs 0.95), which is why the RHP prints P/E as 'N.A.'.

62.00% of the Total Network — 32 of 45 assets, 36.32 msf — was acquired from the Promoters and their related entities, 25 assets in Fiscal 2025 and 6 in Fiscal 2026, and the financial picture presented in the Business and Risk Factors chapters rests on proforma statements that assume those Acquisition Transactions took effect from April 1, 2023, about which the RHP states 'the degree of reliance placed by investors on our Proforma Financial Information should be limited'.

Statutory audit exceptions on the books of account run across the group in both audited years: for FY2026 the auditors are unable to comment on the audit trail at database level for the Holding Company and 35 subsidiaries for want of SOC reports, and the feature was not enabled throughout the year for 12 subsidiaries; for FY2025 the back-up of electronic books of account was not kept daily on servers physically located in India for the Holding Company and 31 subsidiaries, and the prior-year audit trail was not preserved for 4 subsidiaries and 14 newly incorporated subsidiaries.

The Company states it is 'unable to trace the title devolution for periods up to 30 years prior to the acquisition' of certain land parcels, relying on revenue records the RHP itself says may not be reliable, alongside named defects — 8.71 of 14.77 acres at MWC categorised 'Anadheenam' with conveyance and mortgage restrictions, 41.51 acres at Chakan V categorised forest land, 3.42 msf (5.84% of Total Network) at Dobbaspet I from KIADB with third-party claims on compensation adequacy and devolution of title, and mismatches between the Industrial Development Boards' own acquisition notifications and payment receipts.

Litigation against the Subsidiaries aggregates Rs 932.11 million across 27 material civil, 17 tax and 4 statutory or regulatory matters, and the Company states no provisions have been made for outstanding matters. The Materiality Threshold adopted is Rs 90.77 million, being 5% of average absolute PAT of the preceding three years, the lowest of the three permitted tests against 2% of turnover (Rs 138.28 million) and 2% of net worth (Rs 935.23 million).

The statutory auditor resigned mid-cycle on a stated independence ground: Walker Chandiok & Co LLP resigned on March 5, 2025 because the Company proposed to avail non-audit services that could impair independence; M S K C & Associates LLP was appointed on April 25, 2025 to fill the casual vacancy and S G C O & Co. LLP was appointed joint auditor on November 13, 2025. FEMA non-compliance is acknowledged and partly unremedied at the RHP date: late submission fees of Rs 0.13 million on delayed RBI filings for allotments of Equity Shares and Rs 1.89 million on delayed Form FCTRS (four Subsidiaries) and Form DI (35 Subsidiaries) filings, with filings for two Subsidiaries acquired through the Merger Transactions still pending because their erstwhile shareholders' prior filings are unresolved; the RHP gives no assurance the filings will be completed within the prescribed timeline or that no regulatory action or fine will follow.

Delays in payment of statutory dues across all three fiscals, at material scale in Fiscal 2025: TDS of Rs 96.36 million across 48 instances with an average delay of 112 days, GST of Rs 37.64 million across 53 instances, professional tax delayed 467 days on one instance, plus TDS of Rs 8.46 million across 37 instances (FY26) and Rs 6.79 million across 13 instances at 115 days average (FY24), and EPF of Rs 0.33 million across 5 FY26 instances averaging 50 days.

Rs 22,500.00 million of the Rs 26,000.00 million issue leaves the issuer's own P&L largely untouched by the RHP's own admission: because the primary beneficiaries of the repayment object are the Identified Subsidiaries, the RHP states there can be no assurance of any significant improvement in the Company's standalone profitability or cash flows; the Objects have not been appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency; and the identified pool of Rs 46,821.13 million outstanding is about twice the amount to be applied, with no borrower-by-borrower allocation.

Facilities of seven Subsidiaries owed to State Bank of India and Axis Bank Limited — associates of BRLMs SBI Capital Markets Limited and Axis Capital Limited respectively — sit in the repayment pool, including Farukhnagar Logistics Parks LLP Rs 5,189.24 million, FRK II Industrial Park Rs 4,072.50 million, Embassy Industrial Park Hosur Rs 2,949.98 million and Malur Logistics Rs 2,929.62 million outstanding as of March 31, 2026; the RHP concedes there can be no assurance the repayment will not be perceived as a conflict of interest.

The CWC concessions that anchor the in-city strategy are in court: C.W.P. strengths_observed: Occupancy and rental economics on the built portfolio hold up: Committed Occupancy 92.01% (FY24), 93.94% (FY25), 89.88% (FY26) and 93.56% as of May 31, 2026 on a proforma basis across an Operational Network that grew 20.70 to 28.55 msf over the same span; gross rental per square foot per month compounded at 7.69% from April 1, 2023 to May 31, 2026, and 4.78 msf re-leased or renewed since Fiscal 2024 went out at an 11.71% spread over the prior contracts (proforma).

Operating margin is high and rising on both bases: restated EBITDA Rs 6,078.00 mn (FY26), Rs 3,391.17 mn (FY25), Rs 1,515.10 mn (FY24) on revenue from operations of Rs 6,913.81 / 3,902.86 / 2,288.61 mn, an EBITDA Margin of 79.16% / 77.19% / 61.71% as printed by the RHP; proforma EBITDA Rs 6,050.22 mn (FY26) and Rs 5,015.70 mn (FY25) on proforma revenue of Rs 6,913.81 mn and Rs 6,094.23 mn.

Operating cash generation is positive and scaling in every year: restated net cash from operating activities Rs 4,640.73 mn (FY26), Rs 2,351.38 mn (FY25) and Rs 1,192.77 mn (FY24), against cash generated from operations of Rs 4,807.42 / 2,317.16 / 1,219.62 mn.

The issue materially de-levers the group as disclosed: Rs 22,500.00 million of the Rs 26,000.00 million pure fresh issue repays or prepays borrowings of the Company and 16 named Identified Subsidiaries, which the RHP states takes total borrowings from Rs 68,843.41 million to Rs 46,343.41 million and debt-equity from 1.18 times to 0.55 times on a restated basis (1.22 times to 0.56 times proforma). There is no Offer for Sale, so no promoter takes cash off the table in this issue.

Development runway is already on owned, largely freehold land rather than to be bought: land bank of 2,193.07 acres across 45 assets, of which 1,691.08 acres (77.11%) is freehold, 431.37 acres (19.67%) leasehold and 70.62 acres (3.22%) held under a 45-year CWC concession; Development Network of 30.03 msf (7.22 msf Near Term Deliveries, 22.81 msf Planned Projects) stated to be delivered over the next four to five years.

Delivery track record on the recent build is disclosed in physical terms: 11.93 msf of new facilities delivered across 19 assets between Fiscal 2024 and May 31, 2026 (proforma), and 2.57 msf pre-contracted to customers across eight locations as of May 31, 2026 before completion.

Customer base is institutional and widening: 79 customers (FY24), 95 (FY25), 114 (FY26) and 118 as of May 31, 2026 on a proforma basis; 54.05% of the committed Operational Network is contracted to Fortune 500 companies including end tenants of 3PL clients, 12 customers occupy more than one asset, and 40.65% of incremental area contracted since Fiscal 2024 came through repeat engagements. The RHP states no top-10 customer discontinued in Fiscals 2026, 2025 or 2024.

In-city position is the hardest part of the portfolio to replicate: 17 in-city centers with 6.91 msf potential, of which three are operational at 0.79 msf and 100.00% Committed Occupancy as of May 31, 2026, including 13 sites secured from Central Warehousing Corporation on 45-year design-build-finance-operate-transfer concessions.

Insurance cover exceeds the tangible asset base in all three years, unlike many capital-heavy issuers: restated sum insured Rs 59,179.12 / 50,217.30 / 24,778.97 mn against total tangible assets of Rs 49,285.86 / 42,107.14 / 18,785.44 mn, i.e. coverage of 120.07% / 119.26% / 131.91%, with uninsured assets of Rs 1,343.93 / 1,142.83 / 41.09 mn.

Credit standing did not deteriorate through the leverage build: facility-level ratings run from IND BBB/Stable to Crisil AA-/Stable (including Crisil AA-/Stable on Greenbase Horizon Industrial Park Oragadam lease rental discounting loans of Rs 1,100.00 mn, Rs 1,000.00 mn and Rs 4,000.00 mn, all dated September 11, 2025), and the RHP states there was no downgrade in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 and no breach of financial covenants or default notice in those years.

Sustainability and specification standing are certified rather than asserted: 5-Star GRESB rating with a participation score above 90 in its inaugural assessment, and 91.85% of the Operational Network IGBC Platinum certified as of May 31, 2026.

Cash and near-cash on the balance sheet is substantial ahead of the issue: cash and cash equivalents Rs 6,378.35 million and other bank balances Rs 10,137.50 million as of March 31, 2026, with monetary assets of Rs 26,421.17 million reducing gross borrowings of Rs 68,607.38 million to net borrowings of Rs 42,186.21 million as printed under Financial Indebtedness.
